_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 50: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. No harmonised standard is requested for Article 50. The Commission adopted Guidelines on the implementation of the transparency obligations for certain AI systems under Article 50 on 20 July 2026. The Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content was published on 10 June 2026; the Commission and the Board have confirmed that it is an adequate voluntary tool for the marking and labelling obligations it covers.

scope_note: Art. 50 applies to certain AI systems, whether or not they are high-risk: providers of AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons (paragraph 1) and of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content (paragraph 2); deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems (paragraph 3) and of AI systems that generate or manipulate deep fakes or text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest (paragraph 4). Each paragraph has its own exceptions. Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026 (Art. 113); providers of AI systems generating synthetic content that were placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with Art. 50(2) by 2 December 2026 (Art. 111(4)).

requirements.title: Human Interaction Disclosure
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use. This does not apply to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence (Article 50(1)). The information MUST be provided in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction and MUST conform to the applicable accessibility requirements (Article 50(5)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 50(1) is a provider obligation: the system must be designed and developed so that natural persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system; Art. 50(5) requires the information 'in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure'. This applies to chatbots, virtual assistants, AI customer service, AI-powered phone systems, and any conversational AI.
acceptable_implementations: Persistent banner or label: 'You are interacting with an AI system'
Initial disclosure message at conversation start
API response header (e.g. X-AI-Generated: true) that enables downstream applications to show the disclosure; on its own it does not inform the natural person
not_acceptable: Disclosure buried in terms of service only

Disclosure given only after the first interaction (Art. 50(5)); a one-time disclosure that disappears may also fall short where the context calls for ongoing awareness (Commission Guidelines C(2026) 5054, paragraphs 37 and 40)
No disclosure on the assumption that the AI nature is obvious, without assessing it from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect natural person
requirements.exception: Disclosure is not required where it is obvious 'from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use' that the person is interacting with an AI system (e.g., a clearly labelled AI game character). The obligation also does not apply to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence (Art. 50(1)). The obligation, and with it the reliance on the exception, lies with the provider; the Commission Guidelines C(2026) 5054 (paragraphs 42 and 45) state that providers 'will need to assess and demonstrate' obviousness and that the exception should be interpreted restrictively.

requirements.title: Synthetic Content Marking
requirements.requirement: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content MUST ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Providers MUST ensure their technical solutions are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as this is technically feasible, taking into account the specificities and limitations of various types of content, the costs of implementation and the generally acknowledged state of the art. The obligation does not apply to the extent the AI systems perform an assistive function for standard editing or do not substantially alter the input data provided by the deployer or the semantics thereof, or where authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences (Article 50(2)). Providers of such AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 MUST comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026 (Article 111(4)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 50(2) requires that AI-generated content is marked in a way that can be detected by other systems. This enables downstream verification and prevents deceptive use of AI-generated content.
requirements.recommended_standard: C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity)

c2pa_details.description: C2PA provides a technical standard for certifying the source and provenance of media content. It embeds cryptographically signed metadata (manifests) into content files.
key_features: Hardware-binding capability (aligns with ComplianceLint hardware verification approach)
Open standard with broad industry adoption
c2pa_details.eu_alignment: C2PA is not named in the Regulation or in the Commission Guidelines C(2026) 5054 on Article 50. The Guidelines (paragraph 73) mention cryptographic methods for proving provenance and authenticity among possible techniques and state that providers are not required to record or keep a full provenance chain; C2PA is one possible implementation.

acceptable_implementations: C2PA manifest embedding in generated media files
IPTC metadata fields indicating AI generation (DigitalSourceType: trainedAlgorithmicMedia)
SynthID or similar robust watermarking for images
Structured metadata header for AI-generated text (e.g., X-AI-Generated: true, AI-Content-Declaration header)
EXIF/XMP metadata with AI generation flag
not_acceptable: Marking that is easily stripped or removed
Marking only in filename or folder structure

requirements.title: Emotion Recognition / Biometric Categorization Disclosure
requirements.requirement: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system MUST inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system, and MUST process the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable. The obligation does not apply to AI systems used for biometric categorisation and emotion recognition which are permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, and in accordance with Union law (Article 50(3)). The information MUST be provided in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first exposure and MUST conform to the applicable accessibility requirements (Article 50(5)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 50(3) requires disclosure when AI is used for emotion detection or biometric categorization. This is a deployer obligation (not provider), reflecting the sensitivity of these applications. Emotion recognition in the areas of workplace and education institutions is prohibited under Art. 5(1)(f), except where the AI system is intended for medical or safety reasons.
acceptable_implementations: Clear signage in physical spaces where system operates
In-app notification before emotion/biometric processing begins
Consent flow that explains what biometric data is processed
Privacy notice specifically mentioning emotion recognition
requirements.gdpr_intersection: Art. 50(3) requires deployers to process the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable. It names no particular article of those acts; the information duties of Articles 13 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 apply under those acts themselves.

requirements.title: Deep Fake and Public-Interest Text Disclosure
requirements.requirement: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake MUST disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest MUST disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated (Article 50(4)). The information MUST be provided in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first exposure and MUST conform to the applicable accessibility requirements (Article 50(5)). The exceptions and the limitation for artistic, creative, satirical or fictional works are listed below.
requirements.rationale: Art. 50(4) targets deep fakes, defined in Art. 3(60) as 'AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful', and AI-generated or manipulated text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest. Both are deployer obligations.
acceptable_implementations: Clear label on content: 'This content was generated/manipulated by AI'
C2PA manifest indicating manipulation, together with a disclosure the viewer can perceive (a machine-readable manifest alone is not a clear and distinguishable disclosure to natural persons)
Metadata disclosure in content distribution, together with a disclosure the viewer can perceive
exceptions: Where the content forms part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme, the obligation is not lifted but limited to 'disclosure of the existence of such generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work' (Art. 50(4), first subparagraph)

The deep-fake obligation does not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offence (Art. 50(4), first subparagraph). The Regulation contains no exception for cases where disclosure would affect the exercise of a fundamental right. The deployer obligations of Art. 50(4) do not apply to deployers who are natural persons using AI systems in the course of a purely personal non-professional activity (Art. 2(10)).

The text obligation does not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences or where the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication of the content (Art. 50(4), second subparagraph)

chatbot_indicators: Conversational UI components (chat bubbles, message input)
Integration with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
content_generation_indicators: Image generation APIs (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Midjourney)
emotion_recognition_indicators: Emotion detection library imports (e.g., fer, deepface emotion)

scoring.compliant: All applicable R01-R04 requirements met for the system's scope
scoring.partial: Some transparency measures in place but incomplete (e.g., disclosure exists but no machine-readable marking)
scoring.non_compliant: No transparency measures detected for an AI system that clearly falls under Art. 50
scoring.not_applicable: System is not intended to interact directly with natural persons, does not generate synthetic audio, image, video or text content, is not an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system, and is not used to generate or manipulate deep fakes or text published to inform the public on matters of public interest
